title: Transient Capacity Insights and SKU Mapping Spec
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview

Purpose: This design spec defines a product-facing telemetry and SKU-mapping surface for transient (preemptible / spot) capacity. The intent is to make transient capacity economically discoverable, actionable, and auditable for both the Redwood Console and billing pipelines. The spec covers data model, UX artifacts, SLO implications, rollout strategy, and pricing integration.

Scope
- Surface-level: Console insights, API endpoints, and pricing SKU mapping.
- Infra-level: Scheduler and capacity-manager integrations.
- Billing-level: Mapping to crediting and refunds for preemptions.
- Excluded: Long-term committed capacity pricing changes and marketplace 3rd-party reselling.

Background and motivation
Redwood offers transient capacity to reduce customer unit cost and enable bursty workloads. Currently transient capacity is opaque: customers cannot easily see the effective unit-price, eviction risk for a request, or how a given tenant’s traffic maps to transient SKUs. This results in customer confusion during incidents, poor preemption budgeting, and lost opportunities to optimize routing. This spec enables transparent mapping (requests -> transient SKU -> telemetry) and attaches economic primitives (credits, tiers) so the product surface can recommend fallback and budget adjustments.

Key objectives
1) Provide real-time request-level and tenant-level telemetry that shows: allocated capacity type, transient SKU id, effective per-token cost, preemption probability score.
2) Establish a canonical SKU namespace for transient capacity with semantic labels (e.g., sku:transient-gpu-a100-40gb-spot-v2).
3) Wire SKU metadata into billing and Optimize recommendations so customers see accurate cost delta between reserved and transient.
4) Define SLOs and graceful-fallback policies for services using transient capacity.
5) Roll out in staged fashion: telemetry-only -> read-only SKU mapping -> active routing & billing integration.

Product requirements (high level)
- RQ-1: Telemetry must expose the following per-request fields in trace/provenance: allocated_node_id, capacity_class (reserved | burst | transient), transient_sku_id, eviction_risk_score (0.0-1.0), effective_token_cost_usd (decimal).
- RQ-2: Console shall display tenant-level trends with at least 90 days retention for transient events: preemptions/day, transient-utilization, median-latency-by-capacity-class.
- RQ-3: Billing pipeline must accept SKU tags and attach them to usage events so refunds/credits can be applied for preemptions within configured windows.
- RQ-4: Optimize recommendations must include a ‘transient-fit’ indicator that estimates cost savings and expected preemption impact for a tenant’s recent traffic profile.

Data model and canonical SKU namespace
We propose a compact, human-readable SKU name format: sku:<capacity_type>-<gpu>-<mem>-<class>-v<version>. Examples: sku:transient-gpu-a100-40gb-spot-v2, sku:burst-gpu-a10-24gb-burst-v1. SKU metadata attributes (exposed via SKU catalog API and stored as SKU tags): labels (list), max_burst_qps, average_preemption_rate, base_usd_per_token, region_affinity, compatible_models (list).

Sample SKU catalog entry (YAML snippet):

---
sku_id: "sku:transient-gpu-a100-40gb-spot-v2"
labels: ["transient","preemptible","a100-40gb"]
base_usd_per_token: "0.00002"
average_preemption_rate_1h: "0.012"
region_affinity: "us-west-2"
compatible_models: ["gpt-3.5-redwood-1","redwood-llama3-8b"]
max_burst_qps: "480"
---

Telemetry surface and APIs
- New fields added to request provenance event (JSON): allocated_node_id, capacity_class, transient_sku_id, eviction_risk_score, token_cost_usd, preemption_marker (boolean).
- Trace ingestion: sampler needs to preserve SKU metadata for sampled traces; a lightweight indexer will attach SKU metadata to the request id for lookups without bloating trace payloads.
- Query API: /api/v1/telemetry/sku-usage?tenant_id={}&start={}&end={} returns time-series of transient consumption and effective cost deltas.

Observability and SLOs
SLOs for transient-backed routes are intentionally lower than reserved-backed routes because of preemptions; this spec defines observable thresholds and recommended fallbacks.
- SLO-T1 (availability for reserved-backed routes): 99.95% p99 success rate per calendar month.
- SLO-T2 (availability for transient-backed routes): 99.0% p99 success rate per calendar month.
- Alerting thresholds (proactive): if tenant transient_preemptions_rate_1h > 0.03 (3%) trigger capacity-advisory alert in Console and send paging to Router-Stewards team when > 0.1.
- Eviction risk score aggregation: the system publishes per-tenant eviction_risk_rolling_avg_30m; if > 0.25, Recommend switch to reserved or increase fallback budget.

Fallback and routing policy specification
Default policy for customer routes that allow transient: 
1) Attempt to place on transient SKU if predicted latency impact < 10% and eviction_risk_score < 0.15.
2) If preemption occurs mid-request: failover step -> if model supports checkpoint/resume then attempt auto-resume against warm reserved capacity within 250ms; otherwise return graceful degrade response defined by route-level degrade_policy.
3) For long-running sessions (conversational workflows with > 1280 tokens), prefer reserved allocation unless transient preference explicitly set by tenant.

Billing and pricing integration
- Each transient SKU will map to a pricing SKU in the billing catalog. Billing events will include sku_id and a preemption_flag.
- Preemption credit rules (configurable per-customer for first 90s of execution window): full-credit for requests preempted before completion under transient SKUs if preemption_flag=true and eviction_risk_score >= 0.05.
- Example mapping table (described):
  - transient SKU "sku:transient-gpu-a100-40gb-spot-v2" -> pricing_sku "prc:transient-a100-40-v2" -> base_credit_policy "partial" -> default_credit_pct_on_preempt 100 for completion<90s; 50 for completion 90-300s.

Optimize recommendations and Console UX
Console features to be delivered:
- SKU Insights panel (per-tenant): slice by transient vs reserved, show median effective_token_cost_usd, preemption_rate, and suggested budget delta.
- Queryable timeline: hover to see SKU changes and per-request sample traces.
- Cost-simulation widget: slider to change transient_share from 0-100% and display projected monthly spend and estimated preemption events.

Implementation design (engineering details)
- Scheduler integration (runtime-scheduler team): tag allocations with transient_sku_id and eviction_risk_score; expose k/v cache for quick SKU-to-pricing lookup.
- Ingress/router: when making placement decision call SKU-based cost estimator microservice (cost-estimator v1). If route is TTL-sensitive, apply an aggressive reserved-favoring heuristic.
- Telemetry indexer: lightweight service that stores per-tenant SKU aggregates in Cassandra for 90-day retention and ships metrics to Prometheus/Thanos.
- Billing ingestion: Kafka topic "usage.sku.events" augmented with sku_id and preemption_flag. Billing pipelines will join usage events with SKU catalog snapshots for final priced records.

Operational runbook (high-level)
On detection of elevated preemption rates or credit debt:
1) Pager triggers to Router-Stewards and Billing-Stewards.
2) Temporary mitigation: set tenant transient_share to 0% (console toggle) and trigger warm reserved allocation.
3) Recompute affected invoices and apply refunds when applicable.
4) Postmortem: capture timeline using SKU trace index, compute cost impact, and recommend policy changes.

Security and compliance notes
- SKU catalog does not contain PII. SKU events must not leak customer prompt content. Traces associated with preemption investigations require access control; add a new role 'sku-investigator' with audit logging.

Rollout plan and milestones
Phase 0 (telemetry-only) - 4 weeks: emit SKU fields and console read-only SKU insights, no routing changes, no billing tags.
Phase 1 (read-only SKU mapping) - 6 weeks: SKU catalog public, query APIs enabled, console cost-sim widget live. Billing still unaffected.
Phase 2 (billing integration & soft routing) - 8 weeks: usage events carry sku_id, preemption_flag is emitted; billing applies credits in sandbox mode for pilot accounts. Soft routing experiments enabled for low-risk tenants.
Phase 3 (full routing + commercial launch) - 6 weeks: SKU-backed routing enabled broadly, billing credits in production, docs and support playbooks published.

Roles and ownership
- Product owner: Maya Chen (Product)
- Scheduler & runtime owner: Jonas Meyer (Eng - Serving Runtime)
- Telemetry & console owner: Sofia Alvarez (Eng - Platform)
- Billing owner: Ahmed Nasser (Finance & Billing)
- SRE escalation: Router-Stewards oncall (eng-sre)

Acceptance criteria (must-pass)
- AC-1: Telemetry events include transient_sku_id for 99% of transient-backed requests in pilot.
- AC-2: Console SKU Insights load < 500ms for tenant with < 10M monthly tokens.
- AC-3: Billing pipeline receives and processes sku_id events during sandbox pilot and refunds are computed consistent with policy.
- AC-4: No regression in reserved-route p99 latency (difference < 2%) after routing changes.

Open questions and tradeoffs
- Q1: How aggressive should default credit policies be for enterprise customers with custom contracts? (Product + Billing decision required.)
- Q2: Should eviction_risk_score be exposed to end-users as a numeric value or only as qualitative categories (low/medium/high)? Exposing numeric score aids programmatic routing but can confuse customers.
- Q3: Cost of additional trace indexing vs. storage retention window; target 90 days but might reduce to 30 days if index cost is high.

Migration and deprecation notes
- Existing opaque transient tags will be deprecated and replaced by transient_sku_id. Migration flag 'sku-migration-phase' will be used. All services must support old transient flag for 3 months after Phase 1.

Release notes (v0.1)
- 2027-01-18: Initial published specification describing SKU namespace, telemetry fields, billing hooks, and phased rollout plan. Telemetry-only pilot launched for internal tenants.

Appendices
A: Example request provenance JSON (trimmed)
{
  "request_id": "r-0a1b2c3d4e",
  "tenant_id": "t-9f8e7d6c",
  "capacity_class": "transient",
  "transient_sku_id": "sku:transient-gpu-a100-40gb-spot-v2",
  "eviction_risk_score": "0.078",
  "token_cost_usd": "0.000021"
}

B: Console mock (text description)
- Top-level summary: monthly transient spend, transient % of total tokens, preemptions per 1k requests.
- SKU table: columns {sku_id, label, avg_cost_usd_per_token, preemption_rate_1h, compatibility, action} with an action to ‘convert to reserved’ or ‘open soft-routing trial’.

C: Compliance checklist
- Ensure sku-investigator role configured in IAM.
- Audit logs for any manual billing credit applied.
